title: _get_constraint_data hanging with unicode table names

labels.name: performance
labels.description: where performance can be improved.  add "bug" only if it's a performance degradation

body:
This is in reference to the following questions:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/sqlalchemy/l1ttIRVSMac
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50927998/sqlalchemy-oracle-get-constraint-data-method-hanging-with-unicode-table-names

Problem:
The _get_constraint_data takes a long time (100+ seconds, depending on a variety of factors) to return results for the Oracle dialect.

Cause:
It appears as though the 'info_cache' dict that populates the variables for the _get_constraint_data query is always using unicode characters. Whether this is occurring in SqlAlchemy or cx_Oracle code is unclear. What is clear is that Oracle processes the query slower because of this.

Potential Workaround:
After speaking with the db admin for our Oracle server, he suggested replacing the "all_" tables with their "user_" alternatives (perhaps when just having an owner defined?). 

Here's what my version of dialects/oracle/base.py -- _get_constraint_data looks like:
```python
 @reflection.cache
def _get_constraint_data(self, connection, table_name, schema=None,
                         dblink='', **kw):

    params = {'table_name': table_name}

    text = (
        "SELECT"
        "\nac.constraint_name,"  # 0
        "\nac.constraint_type,"  # 1
        "\nloc.column_name AS local_column,"  # 2
        "\nrem.table_name AS remote_table,"  # 3
        "\nrem.column_name AS remote_column,"  # 4
        "\nrem.owner AS remote_owner,"  # 5
        "\nloc.position as loc_pos,"  # 6
        "\nrem.position as rem_pos,"  # 7
        "\nac.search_condition,"  # 8
        "\nac.delete_rule"  # 9
        "\nFROM user_constraints%(dblink)s ac," # Change starts here
        "\nuser_cons_columns%(dblink)s loc,"  #
        "\nuser_cons_columns%(dblink)s rem" # Change ends here
        "\nWHERE ac.table_name = :table_name"
        "\nAND ac.constraint_type IN ('R','P', 'U', 'C')"
    )

    if schema is not None:
        params['owner'] = schema
        text += "\nAND ac.owner = :owner"

    text += (
        "\nAND ac.owner = loc.owner"
        "\nAND ac.constraint_name = loc.constraint_name"
        "\nAND ac.r_owner = rem.owner(+)"
        "\nAND ac.r_constraint_name = rem.constraint_name(+)"
        "\nAND (rem.position IS NULL or loc.position=rem.position)"
        "\nORDER BY ac.constraint_name, loc.position"
    )

    text = text % {'dblink': dblink}
    rp = connection.execute(sql.text(text), **params)
    constraint_data = rp.fetchall()
    return constraint_data
```
